about_blocks.text: HOPE Be The Cure: a five-bed residential addiction program in Innisfil, Ontario
about_blocks.html: HOPE Be The Cure: a five-bed residential addiction program in Innisfil, Ontario

about_blocks.text: HOPE Be The Cure is a private residential program for adults with alcohol and drug addiction. It runs out of a house at 752 Pinegrove Avenue in Innisfil, a short drive south of Barrie, and takes no more than five clients at a time. The centre gives its staffing ratio as 1 to 3, so the people working with you get to know you well.
about_blocks.html: HOPE Be The Cure is a private residential program for adults with alcohol and drug addiction. It runs out of a house at 752 Pinegrove Avenue in Innisfil, a short drive south of Barrie, and takes no more than five clients at a time. The centre gives its staffing ratio as 1 to 3, so the people working with you get to know you well.

about_blocks.text: Most of the week is built around counselling. Each client has two 60-minute one-to-one sessions a week with a certified addiction counsellor, and interactive group workshops happen every day, some at the house and some off site. The centre lists cognitive behavioural therapy, psychotherapy, psycho-educational workshops and a relapse prevention program, which focuses on spotting triggers and cravings before they turn into a slip.

about_blocks.text: The program is also 12-step based. Clients are expected to attend at least three 12-step meetings a week. Alongside that, there is a long list of wellness activities: exercise, yoga, meditation, breathwork, reiki, walks on local trails and lakeside paths, and an organic garden whose produce goes into cooking classes. The menu changes every week.

about_blocks.text: The house itself is a plain family home rather than a clinic. Photos on the centre's profile show an open kitchen with a long dining table, a screened porch, a bright living room and bedrooms with two single beds. Clients can have a private or a shared room, and local trails, forest and the Lake Simcoe shoreline are close by for walks.

about_blocks.text: The program takes alcohol, opioid, fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine addiction, and its recovery.com profile also lists benzodiazepines, heroin and ecstasy. Men and women attend together. The centre does not list medical detox on site, so anyone who needs withdrawal management should raise that on the first call.

about_blocks.text: Support continues after discharge. Graduates can join a weekly 90-minute in-person aftercare group led by a certified addictions counsellor, and families have their own weekly virtual support meeting. HOPE Be The Cure is private pay, with fees charged monthly, and admissions answers the phone 24 hours a day at 647-697-8076.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About HOPE Be The Cure

faqs.question: What kind of program is HOPE Be The Cure?

answer_blocks.text: HOPE Be The Cure is a private residential addiction program, so clients live at the house while they are in treatment. It has five beds and a staffing ratio the centre gives as 1 to 3. Former clients and families can also join weekly aftercare and family support groups.
answer_blocks.html: HOPE Be The Cure is a private residential addiction program, so clients live at the house while they are in treatment. It has five beds and a staffing ratio the centre gives as 1 to 3. Former clients and families can also join weekly aftercare and family support groups.

faqs.question: Where is HOPE Be The Cure located?

answer_blocks.text: The house is at 752 Pinegrove Avenue in Innisfil, Ontario, in Simcoe County on the south side of Barrie. Toronto is about an hour away by Highway 400, and Barrie is roughly 15 to 20 minutes by car. Call admissions before you travel so they can plan your arrival.

faqs.question: How much does HOPE Be The Cure cost?

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not publish its prices, and its recovery.com profile says to call for rates. Its client agreement describes a monthly service fee paid in advance, which does not cover prescription medication or outside therapists. Ask admissions for the current fee on your first call.

faqs.question: How long does the program last?

answer_blocks.text: HOPE Be The Cure does not publish a fixed program length. Fees are charged by the month, and the client agreement asks for 30 days written notice before leaving. Admissions can tell you how long most clients stay.
